name: web_search
description:
Purpose: Perform web searches and return
LLM-friendly results, including excerpts that are usually sufficient to
answer directly without a follow-up fetch.

Ideal Use Cases:
- Answering questions that require fresh or current information
- Research, comparison, documentation, and troubleshooting questions
- Broad tasks where multiple `search_queries` can be issued in a single call

For multiple independent objectives, make one web_search call per objective
concurrently. Put related query variations for the same objective in a single
call's search_queries list.

name: web_fetch
description:
Purpose: Fetch and extract relevant content
from specific web URLs. Use only when web_search excerpts are insufficient
for the task at hand.

Ideal Use Cases:
- The user asked about a specific URL or page
- You need exact wording or quotes that excerpts may have truncated
- You need full-page analysis (long article, document, or page structure)
- web_search excerpts are conflicting or clearly insufficient to answer

For multiple independent extraction objectives, make separate web_fetch calls
concurrently. Put related URLs that share one objective in a single call.

name: web_decisions
description:
Answer typed questions about a subject using current web evidence. Call this
only when the user asks for web_decisions or Parallel Decisions by name, or asks
for a probability, a pick among options they give, or a score on a scale they
give. For other questions, including yes/no facts, use web_search; if this tool
seems a better fit, suggest it to the user instead of calling it. Describe the
subject in `state` as JSON, for example {"company": "Acme"}. Name each question
in `questions`; its answer comes back under the same name, with call-level
citations. Question types:
- noul: the probabilit

name: find_verticals
description:
Find specialized data sources (verticals) for a request, beyond web search:
preprints (bioRxiv, medRxiv), bioactive compounds (ChEMBL), clinical trials (ClinicalTrials.gov), Medicare national coverage (CMS), US healthcare providers (NPI Registry), biomedical literature (PubMed) and places and local businesses. Returns every vertical you can use, best match first, with its id and
price per call in US dollars, by `mode` when it has one. The best matches also
carry their full description and input schema. Then call search_vertical with an
id and arguments that match its input schema. If no verti

name: search_vertical
description:
Query one vertical by its id from find_verticals, such as
`pubmed.search_articles` or `clinical_trials.search_trials`. `arguments` must
match the vertical's input schema. Returns the source's records and citations.

name: image_search
description:
Find images on the web. Returns direct image URLs with the
page each appears on, its title, and pixel dimensions when known. Results link to
images; they do not describe them. Use web_search for information about a
subject.

name: send_feedback
description:
Report a problem with Parallel to the Parallel team. Use it when, while
working with Parallel, you see any of these:
- A Parallel tool returned an error you didn't cause: a 5xx, a timeout, or a
  rate limit you didn't expect.
- Results were wrong, irrelevant, stale or missing something you know exists:
  a wrong date or number, an excerpt the page doesn't support, an empty fetch of
  a page that has content.
- Parallel's docs, tool descriptions and behavior disagree, or you couldn't work
  out how to call a tool.
- An evaluation, benchmark or comparison you ran shows Parallel doing worse than

name: firecrawl_scrape
description:
Scrape one URL and return its content: markdown by default, or HTML, links, screenshots, branding data, or a targeted answer. Use it when the request identifies a page and needs its content or defined fields: the user gives a URL or names a page or PDF and wants it read or summarized, or wants prices, specs, contact details or a table from it. Use `firecrawl_search` when additional web sources are needed; on an authenticated session, `firecrawl_map` lists a site's URLs and `firecrawl_crawl` collects a set of pages. `url` may omit the scheme (`example.com/page`); it is read as https.

Firecraw

name: firecrawl_search
description: Use this when you need current or specific information from the web: recent events, latest releases and versions, prices, people and companies, statistics, or any fact that may have changed since your training data or that you are not sure of. Returns ranked results with query-relevant highlights; each web result is a title, URL, and description. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. `includeDomains` and `excludeDomains` are mutually exclusive hostname filters; categories limit result types to `rese

name: firecrawl_parse
description:
Parse one supported document into markdown, HTML, links, summary, targeted answers, or JSON matching a schema. Supported inputs include common HTML, PDF, Word, RTF, OpenDocument, and spreadsheet files; PDF parsing can be bounded with `pdfOptions.maxPages`.

Local MCP reads `filePath` from the server filesystem. Hosted MCP uses two calls: first provide `filePath` to receive upload instructions, upload locally, then call again with the returned `uploadRef`; do not send both fields together. Remote web URLs belong in `firecrawl_scrape`.

Set `redactPII` to request redaction of personally identif

name: web_search_exa
description:
Search the web for any topic and get clean, ready-to-use content.

      Best for: Finding current information, news, facts, people, companies, or answering questions about any topic.
      Returns: Clean text content from top search results.

      Query tips:
      describe the ideal page, not keywords. "blog post comparing React and Vue performance" not "React vs Vue".
      Use category:people / category:company to search through Linkedin profiles / companies respectively.
      If highlights are insufficient, follow up with web_fetch_exa on the best URLs.

name: web_fetch_exa
description:
Read a webpage's full content as clean markdown. Use after web_search_exa when highlights are insufficient or to read any URL.

Best for: Extracting full content from known URLs. Batch multiple URLs in one call.
Returns: Clean text content and metadata from the page(s).

name: primer
description: Current time, user location and network environment for the session. Use before answering anything time- or location-dependent.

name: guess_datetime_url
description: Guess when a page was published or last updated, with a confidence score. Checks HTTP headers, metadata, Schema.org, visible dates, feeds and sitemaps.

name: capture_screenshot_url
description: Screenshot a page as base64 JPEG. Use when the page must be seen rather than read.

name: read_url
description: Fetch a URL (page or PDF) as clean markdown. Pass `question` to get only the passages answering it instead of the whole page - far cheaper than reading the full body into context.

name: search_web
description: Search the web. Returns titles, URLs and search-engine snippets.

name: search_arxiv
description: Search arXiv preprints (physics, maths, CS, quantitative biology and finance).

name: search_ssrn
description: Search SSRN working papers (social science, economics, law, finance, management).

name: search_jina_blog
description: Search Jina AI's news and blog at jina.ai/news: product announcements, model releases, technical write-ups.

name: search_images
description: Search the web for images. Returns base64 JPEGs by default.

name: sort_by_relevance
description: Rerank documents by relevance to a query, using Jina Reranker.

name: deduplicate_strings
description: Select the top-k semantically distinct strings from a list, dropping near-duplicates.

name: extract_pdf
description: Extract figures, tables and equations from a PDF as images, by arXiv id or URL.

name: resolve-library-id
description:
Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns matching libraries.

You MUST call this function before 'Query Documentation' tool to obtain a valid Context7-compatible library ID UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

Each result includes:
- Library ID: Context7-compatible identifier (format: /org/project)
- Name: Library or package name
- Description: Short summary
- Code Snippets: Number of available code examples
- Source Reputation: Authority indicator (High, Medium, Low, or U

name: query-docs
description:
Retrieves and queries up-to-date documentation and code examples from Context7 for any programming library or framework.

You must call 'Resolve Context7 Library ID' tool first to obtain the exact Context7-compatible library ID required to use this tool, UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

Do not call this tool more than 3 times per question.

If you know the programming language the user is working in, pass it as `language` so the results match their setup.

name: actions_get
description:
Get details about specific GitHub Actions resources.
Use this tool to get details about individual workflows, workflow runs, jobs, and artifacts by their unique IDs.

name: actions_list
description:
Tools for listing GitHub Actions resources.
Use this tool to list workflows in a repository, or list workflow runs, jobs, and artifacts for a specific workflow or workflow run.

name: actions_run_trigger
description: Trigger GitHub Actions workflow operations, including running, re-running, cancelling workflow runs, and deleting workflow run logs.

name: add_automation_to_group
description: Add one existing Automation to one exact group using its live membership version. It refuses to detach or move an Automation that already references another visible or unavailable group, and it never changes the Automation configuration or enabled state.

name: add_comment_to_pending_review
description: Add review comment to the requester's latest pending pull request review. A pending review needs to already exist to call this (check with the user if not sure).

name: add_issue_comment
description: Add a comment and/or reaction to a specific issue or issue comment in a GitHub repository. Use this tool with pull requests as well (in this case pass pull request number as issue_number), but only if user is not asking specifically to add or react to review comments. At least one of body or reaction is required.

name: add_reply_to_pull_request_comment
description: Add a reply and/or reaction to an existing pull request comment. This can create a new comment linked as a reply to the specified comment, add an emoji reaction to the specified comment, or do both. At least one of body or reaction is required.

name: check_dependency_vulnerabilities
description:
Check a list of dependencies for known vulnerabilities using the GitHub Security Advisory Database.
This tool queries the GitHub Advisory Database to find known security vulnerabilities affecting the specified packages.

Use this tool when:
- You want to check if project dependencies have known vulnerabilities
- You are adding a new dependency to a project and should check it is safe before adding to the project

The tool accepts owner, repo, and a list of dependencies with their ecosystems and versions, then returns any matching security advisories with upgrade recommendations where available

name: create_automation
description: Create a Copilot Automation in a repository. Use get_automations_configuration_for_repository to check if automations are enabled for the repository, whether the caller can create automations and what automations configurations are allowed.

name: create_automation_group
description: Create one repository Automation group after explicit user approval. This tool creates only the group; use create_automation and add_automation_to_group for members. It never retries an unconfirmed write or adopts a group by name.

name: create_branch
description: Create a new branch in a GitHub repository

name: create_gist
description: Create a new gist

name: create_or_update_file
description:
Create or update a single file in a GitHub repository. 
If updating, you should provide the SHA of the file you want to update. Use this tool to create or update a file in a GitHub repository remotely; do not use it for local file operations.

To obtain the current blob SHA before updating, call the get_file_contents tool with the same owner, repo, and path, and set its ref parameter to this tool's branch value. The first text result reports the blob SHA for the requested path.

SHA MUST be provided for existing file updates.

name: create_pull_request
description: Create a new pull request in a GitHub repository.

name: create_repository
description: Create a new GitHub repository in your account or specified organization

name: create_repository_ruleset
description: Create a new ruleset at the repository, organization, or enterprise level

name: custom_properties_read
description: Read custom properties at the repository, organization, or enterprise level. At the repository level this returns the property values assigned to a repository; at the organization and enterprise levels it returns the property definitions (schema). Select the level with the 'level' parameter.

name: custom_properties_write
description: Create or update custom properties at the repository, organization, or enterprise level. At the repository level this sets the property values on a repository (the properties must already be defined for the organization). Organization and enterprise definition writes preserve omitted writable fields by reading current definitions immediately before updating; concurrent definition updates remain last-write-wins. Select the level with the 'level' parameter.

name: delete_automation
description: Delete a Copilot Automation from a repository.

name: delete_file
description: Delete a file from a GitHub repository

name: discussion_comment_write
description:
Write operations for discussion comments.
Supports adding top-level comments, replying to existing comments, updating comment content, deleting comments, and marking or unmarking comments as the answer.

name: dismiss_notification
description: Dismiss a notification by marking it as read or done

name: fork_repository
description: Fork a GitHub repository to your account or specified organization

name: get_automation
description: Get a Copilot Automation in a repository.

name: get_automation_group
description: Get one exact repository Automation group and its current visible members. Membership comes from live state; no expected role count or completeness is inferred. No resources are changed.

name: get_automation_revision
description: Get a revision of a Copilot Automation.

name: get_automations_configuration_for_repository
description: Get Copilot Automations configuration for a repository.

name: get_code_quality_finding
description: Get details of a specific code quality finding in a GitHub repository.

name: get_code_scanning_alert
description: Get details of a specific code scanning alert in a GitHub repository.

name: get_commit
description: Get details for a commit from a GitHub repository

name: get_copilot_session_events
description: Read one chronological page of a Copilot session's logs/output as SDK events. Use an explicit session_id from get_copilot_task_status. No polling, waiting, or execution changes. page_size defaults to 50 (maximum 100). Use page_number/next_page_number to traverse every event, including synthetic events. Alternatively pass next_after as after to resume; it may yield an empty page. after and page_number are mutually exclusive. total is the upstream unpaginated event count at this read, not a completion signal. Responses exceeding 4 MiB upstream or 512 KiB of combined serialized MCP content (exclu

name: get_copilot_space
description:
This tool can be used to provide additional context to the chat from a specific Copilot space. If the user mentions the keyword 'Copilot space' with the name and owner of the space, execute this tool.

The response includes a table of contents (TOC) listing all documents in the space, followed by the full content of each document. Documents are separated by markers in the format: '--- Document N: path (size) ---'. When searching for specific information, use grep (or equivalent command) to search across all documents; the separator lines will help identify which document contains the matching

name: get_copilot_task_status
description: Read one current Copilot task-status snapshot by task_id using the invoking caller's access. Use an existing task's UUID, for example from its repository task URL, not an automation_id. Returns Mission Control's task state and timestamps, plus IDs, states, timestamps and recorded errors for every session. States are reported as-is, not interpreted as aggregate success; no primary session is selected. Does not return prompts, transcripts or events, poll, wait for completion, or relaunch work. When available, use get_copilot_session_events with an explicit returned session ID as session_id for e

name: get_dependabot_alert
description: Get details of a specific dependabot alert in a GitHub repository.

name: get_discussion
description: Get a specific discussion by ID

name: get_discussion_comments
description: Get comments from a discussion

name: get_file_contents
description: Get the contents of a file or directory from a GitHub repository

name: get_gist
description: Get gist content of a particular gist, by gist ID

name: get_global_security_advisory
description: Get a global security advisory

name: get_job_logs
description:
Get logs for GitHub Actions workflow jobs.
Use this tool to retrieve logs for a specific job or all failed jobs in a workflow run.
For single job logs, provide job_id. For all failed jobs in a run, provide run_id with failed_only=true.

name: get_label
description: Get a specific label from a repository.

name: get_latest_release
description: Get the latest release in a GitHub repository

name: get_me
description: Get details of the authenticated GitHub user. Use this when a request is about the user's own profile for GitHub. Or when information is missing to build other tool calls.

name: get_notification_details
description: Get detailed information for a specific GitHub notification, always call this tool when the user asks for details about a specific notification, if you don't know the ID list notifications first.

name: get_release_by_tag
description: Get a specific release by its tag name in a GitHub repository

name: get_repository_tree
description: Get the tree structure (files and directories) of a GitHub repository at a specific ref or SHA

name: get_secret_scanning_alert
description: Get details of a specific secret scanning alert in a GitHub repository.

name: get_tag
description: Get details about a specific git tag in a GitHub repository

name: get_team_members
description: Get member usernames of a specific team in an organization. Limited to organizations accessible with current credentials

name: get_teams
description: Get details of the teams the user is a member of. Limited to organizations accessible with current credentials

name: github_support_docs_search
description: Retrieve documentation relevant to answer GitHub product and support questions. Support topics include: GitHub Actions Workflows, Authentication, GitHub Support Inquiries, Pull Request Practices, Repository Maintenance, GitHub Pages, GitHub Packages, GitHub Discussions, Copilot Spaces

name: issue_read
description: Get information about a specific issue in a GitHub repository.

name: issue_write
description: Create a new or update an existing issue in a GitHub repository.

name: label_write
description: Perform write operations on repository labels. To set labels on issues, use the 'update_issue' tool.

name: list_automation_groups
description: List repository Automation groups and the authenticated account identity. Group data comes from live state; a saved link or name does not establish access. Use the returned identity as expected_identity for group mutations. No resources are changed.

name: list_automation_revisions
description: List revisions for a Copilot Automation.

name: list_automations
description: List Copilot Automations for a repository.

name: list_available_automation_tools

name: list_available_automation_triggers
description: List available triggers for Copilot Automations.

name: list_branches
description: List branches in a GitHub repository

name: list_code_scanning_alerts
description: List code scanning alerts in a GitHub repository.

name: list_commits
description: Get list of commits of a branch in a GitHub repository. Returns at least 30 results per page by default, but can return more if specified using the perPage parameter (up to 100).

name: list_copilot_spaces
description: Retrieves the list of Copilot Spaces accessible to the user, including their names and owners.

name: list_dependabot_alerts
description: List dependabot alerts in a GitHub repository.

name: list_discussion_categories
description: List discussion categories with their id and name, for a repository or organisation.

name: list_discussions
description: List discussions for a repository or organisation.

name: list_gists
description: List gists for a user

name: list_global_security_advisories
description: List global security advisories from GitHub.

name: list_issue_fields
description: List issue fields for a repository or organization. Returns field definitions including name, type (text, number, date, single_select), and for single_select fields the list of valid option names. When repo is omitted, returns org-level fields directly.

name: list_issue_types
description: List supported issue types for a repository or its owner organization. When repo is omitted, returns org-level issue types directly.

name: list_issues
description: List issues in a GitHub repository. For pagination, use the 'endCursor' from the previous response's 'pageInfo' in the 'after' parameter.

name: list_label
description: List labels from a repository, ordered by issue count (descending) so the most-used labels are returned first. For pagination, use the 'endCursor' from the previous response's 'pageInfo' in the 'after' parameter.

name: list_notifications
description: Lists all GitHub notifications for the authenticated user, including unread notifications, mentions, review requests, assignments, and updates on issues or pull requests. Use this tool whenever the user asks what to work on next, requests a summary of their GitHub activity, wants to see pending reviews, or needs to check for new updates or tasks. This tool is the primary way to discover actionable items, reminders, and outstanding work on GitHub. Always call this tool when asked what to work on next, what is pending, or what needs attention in GitHub.

name: list_org_repository_security_advisories
description: List repository security advisories for a GitHub organization.

name: list_pull_requests
description: List pull requests in a GitHub repository. If the user specifies an author, then DO NOT use this tool and use the search_pull_requests tool instead.

name: list_releases
description: List releases in a GitHub repository

name: list_repository_collaborators
description: List collaborators of a GitHub repository. Results are paginated; the response includes `nextPage`, `prevPage`, `firstPage`, and `lastPage` fields. To get the next page, use the `nextPage` value as the `page` parameter.

name: list_repository_security_advisories
description: List repository security advisories for a GitHub repository.

name: list_secret_scanning_alerts
description: List secret scanning alerts in a GitHub repository.

name: list_starred_repositories
description: List starred repositories

name: list_tags
description: List git tags in a GitHub repository

name: manage_notification_subscription
description: Manage a notification subscription: ignore, watch, or delete a notification thread subscription.

name: manage_repository_notification_subscription
description: Manage a repository notification subscription: ignore, watch, or delete repository notifications subscription for the provided repository.

name: mark_all_notifications_read
description: Mark all notifications as read

name: merge_pull_request
description: Merge a pull request in a GitHub repository.

name: projects_get
description:
Get details about specific GitHub Projects resources.
Use this tool to get details about individual projects, project fields, project items, and project views by their unique IDs.

name: projects_list
description:
Tools for listing GitHub Projects resources.
Use this tool to list projects for a user or organization, or list project fields, items, views, and status updates for a specific project.

name: projects_write
description: Create and manage GitHub Projects: create projects, add/update/delete items, bulk-update many items at once, manage views, create status updates, and add iteration fields.

name: pull_request_read
description: Get information on a specific pull request in GitHub repository.

name: pull_request_review_write
description:
Create and/or submit, delete review of a pull request.

Available methods:
- create: Create a new review of a pull request. If "event" parameter is provided, the review is submitted. If "event" is omitted, a pending review is created.
- submit_pending: Submit an existing pending review of a pull request. This requires that a pending review exists for the current user on the specified pull request. The "body" and "event" parameters are used when submitting the review.
- delete_pending: Delete an existing pending review of a pull request. This requires that a pending review exists for the curren

name: push_files
description: Push multiple files to a GitHub repository in a single commit

name: remove_automation_from_group
description: Remove one existing Automation from one exact group using its live membership version. It never deletes, disables, or otherwise changes the Automation.

name: repository_ruleset_read
description: Read rulesets at the repository, organization, or enterprise level, and rule suites at the repository or organization level. Select the level with the 'level' parameter and the operation with the 'method' parameter.

name: request_copilot_review
description: Request a GitHub Copilot code review for a pull request. Use this for automated feedback on pull requests, usually before requesting a human reviewer.

name: run_automation
description: Request one real run of one exact Automation for manual or a configured non-manual event supported by Run now; this is not a dry run. For configured events, use get_automation to read the trigger's types and conclusions. Provide type, conclusion, and resource_url explicitly when the event requires them. Events involving issues, pull requests, workflow runs, or discussions require the corresponding URL; comment events require the exact comment permalink. When group_id is supplied, first verify current visible membership. Returns taskId for the requested run. Acceptance does not confirm task cre

name: run_secret_scanning
description:
Scan files, content, or recent changes for secrets such as API keys, passwords, tokens, and credentials.

This tool is intended for targeted scans of specific files, snippets, or diffs provided directly as content. The files parameter accepts either a single string or an array of strings containing raw file contents or diff hunks, and returns detected secrets with their locations and related secret scanning metadata. Content must not be empty. For full repository scanning, other mechanisms are available.

Caveats:

- Only files within the codebase should be scanned. Files outside of the codeba

name: search_code
description: Fast and precise code search across ALL GitHub repositories using GitHub's native search engine. Best for finding exact symbols, functions, classes, or specific code patterns.

name: search_commits
description: Search for commits across GitHub repositories using GitHub's commit search syntax. Useful for finding specific changes, authors, or messages across one or many repositories. Searches the default branch only.

name: search_issues
description: Search issues using natural-language semantic matching. Best for conceptual or paraphrased queries (e.g. "login fails after password reset"). Already scoped to is:issue.

name: search_orgs
description: Find GitHub organizations by name, location, or other organization metadata. Ideal for discovering companies, open source foundations, or teams.

name: search_pull_requests
description: Search for pull requests in GitHub repositories using issues search syntax already scoped to is:pr

name: search_repositories
description: Find GitHub repositories by name, description, readme, topics, or other metadata. Perfect for discovering projects, finding examples, or locating specific repositories across GitHub.

name: search_users
description: Find GitHub users by username, real name, or other profile information. Useful for locating developers, contributors, or team members.

name: semantic_issue_similarity_search
description: Find issues that are semantically similar to a given issue using natural language understanding. Useful for identifying duplicates, related issues, or similar problems.

name: star_repository
description: Star a GitHub repository

name: sub_issue_write
description: Add a sub-issue to a parent issue in a GitHub repository.

name: ui_get
description: Fetch UI data for MCP Apps (labels, assignees, milestones, issue types, branches, issue fields, reviewers).

name: unstar_repository
description: Unstar a GitHub repository

description: Partially update a Copilot Automation. Omitted fields are unchanged; empty strings, arrays, and objects clear fields that support clearing. Use get_automations_configuration_for_repository to check if automations are enabled for the repository, whether the caller can update automations and what automations configurations are allowed.

name: update_gist
description: Update an existing gist

name: update_issue_comment
description: Update the body of an existing issue or pull request conversation comment. This tool cannot update pull request review comments.

name: update_pull_request

name: update_pull_request_branch
description: Update the branch of a pull request with the latest changes from the base branch.
